title: Product Photo and Video Glossary | AIVideosUGC
description: Plain product photo and video terms for your shop, from credits and frame sizes to ad words. Open a term, follow the link, and make the photo or the clip.
eyebrow: Find a Term and Make the File
lead: Explore plain product photo and video terms in one glossary, so you can learn a word, follow the link, and make the file you need.

entries.definition: Credits are spent per job: a photo is 24, and a video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, Premium is $63 for 600, and a failed job returns them.
Aspect ratio is how wide the frame is beside how tall it is. Choose 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 to match the post, then look at the edges after download.
Duration is how long the clip runs, and you can pick 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. A lid closing can stay short, while an unboxing needs the longer cut so both halves fit.
A white background sets the product on plain white and leaves the rest of the frame empty. Start from a sharp photo of the whole item, then read that site's current image rules.
A packshot is a clean product photo with the item standing alone, so a shopper can judge the shape and the surface. It is not a daily scene with extra things or a person.
UGC is a clip that looks like a shopper filmed the product on a phone, and an AI actor can say a line you write. The person on screen is fictional, so say so if the platform asks you to.
B-roll is extra footage of the product, a hand, a close detail, or a daily action. It is not just a person talking to the camera, so the item stays easy to see.
Spark Ads are TikTok ads that boost a post you already put up. You can send a video from here, then set who sees it, the budget, and the permission TikTok asks for.
Retargeting means ads for people who already visited your shop, viewed a product, or left a cart. You make the photo or video here, and the ad account chooses who sees it.
A safe zone is the middle of a social video that people still see. The app covers the edges with buttons and captions, so keep the product and your words away from those edges.
A feed ad is a paid photo or video inside the scrolling list of posts. Make a clear product scene, often square, and type the price so it matches the store today.
Ads Manager is the screen where you choose who sees the ad, the budget, and when it runs. Send the file to TikTok or Meta, or download it and post it yourself.
A product demo is a short video of one useful action, such as a pour or a lid closing. Upload a photo that shows the moving part, then compare the file with the real item.
An unboxing video shows a package opening and the product coming out, in the order you describe. Your photo keeps the item looking like the one you sell, including the box and the paper.
Before-and-after shows the start, then the change a product makes, such as a drawer put in order. Do not promise a medical result or a body change the real item cannot do.
A lifestyle photo puts the product in an everyday place, so a shopper can picture owning it, like a mug beside a book. Compare the file with the real item before you use it.
An on-model photo shows clothes, jewelry, or a bag on a person the tool makes, so you can see the hang and the scale. Keep your size chart beside the picture, since the photo does not measure fit.
A flat lay is a photo from above, with the product and a few other items on a surface. Upload the whole product, and only include things you actually sell.
A swatch is a small sample of a color or a surface beside the product, so a shopper can judge the shade. Make it from your own photos, then add the color name and the price.
A variant is one option a shopper can buy, such as a color, a size, or a surface. Upload a photo for each option you sell, then place that file on the matching option.
A carousel is several slides in one social ad, so people can swipe through products or colors. You make each photo or video here, then set the order and the link in the ad account.
A call to action is the short line that tells someone what to do next, such as shop or view the product. Put it in the spoken line or the captions, and match the price to your store.
AI-generated content is a picture or video the tool creates or changes, rather than a frame you only filmed. Check it against the real item, and do not present a generated person as a buyer.
A caption is words on a video that appear at the right moment, or the written line under a post. Edit them so the price, the date, and any code match the store now.
Spoken narration is the voice you hear on a video, spoken by an AI actor from the line you write. You choose the language by writing that line, and the speech is not a buyer review.
A template is a ready setup for one photo or video, such as a white background, an unboxing, or a short demo. Upload the product photo, follow the notes, and run again for a different setup.

A marketplace listing is the product page you keep on a selling site such as Amazon or Etsy, and that site sets the image slots. Download the files here, then read the current rules before you upload.
DTC means direct to consumer: the brand sells in its own online store, not only on a marketplace. You use the photos and short videos on that store, in posts, in email, and in ads.
An AI actor is a made-up person on screen who can hold, wear, or talk about a product. Pick from 53 AI actors or describe the look, and remember the picture does not replace a size chart.
An AI script is the spoken line the tool writes from the product and the buyer you name, and you can edit every sentence first. The line should only say what the real item does.
An AI voice is the voice an actor uses for the line you write, and you choose the language by writing that line. The voice comes from the tool, not from a buyer recording.
An API lets other software ask for a product photo or a video, and the credit charge matches what you see in the app. A failed job returns the credits.

A batch is several photos or videos from one product photo, each with its own scene or length, and each shows its credit cost first. Download the ones you want, or send a finished file to TikTok or Meta.
The built-in editor changes a finished file without a second app. You can change the spoken line, the captions, the voice, the music, and the person on screen, then download again.
Link to video starts a clip from a public product page, using that page's main image and the product name. It does not copy prices or reviews, so check the file before you post.
The music library is a set of songs you can place under a product video, and swap the song when the mood should change. You still write the spoken line, and you own every word of it.
One-click publish sends a finished photo or video to TikTok or Meta from here, and you can download the file instead. You still set the audience, the budget, and the schedule in the ad account.
Ad cloning means a new ad that follows a look you already like, with your own product in the frame. Start from a template, then swap in the photo of the item you ship.
The AI video agent asks who the product is for, then drafts a script you can edit. You still approve the line before anyone hears it, and it should only say what the real item does.
A/B testing means you show two versions of an ad and keep the one you prefer. Change one piece, such as the opening line, so the comparison stays fair.
Ad text is the words in the ad, meaning the spoken line, the caption, and the offer. Write the offer you are really running, then read it aloud before you post.
Ad spend is the budget you set in the ad account for who sees the ad. The photo or clip you make here spends credits, not that budget.
CTR means click-through rate: how many people clicked after they saw the ad, which you read in the ad account. That count is not a promise about the next ad you make.
CPC means cost per click, the charge in the ad account when someone clicks. The photo or clip you make here spends credits, not that click charge.
Conversion rate counts how many clicks become an order, the way the ad account counts them. Make two ads here, then keep the one you want.
Creative testing means you run more than one opening, scene, or line, then keep the ad you want. Change one piece at a time so you know what changed.
Content marketing is the posts and videos you publish so shoppers learn the product before they buy. Make a short clip from the product photo and post it, with no shoot to book.
A display ad is a paid picture on a website or in an app, outside a social feed. Make that picture here so the product stays easy to see, then post it.
Facebook ads are paid posts that show up on Facebook. A square file or a tall file can run there after you download it, or you can send the file from here.
Deep learning is the training that lets the tool build a picture or a clip from what it has learned. Upload your own photo, skip the shoot, and approve the file before you post.
